challenge.name: The Silent Drift
challenge.description: The production drift monitoring pipeline is broken, leaving the model's input quality unchecked. #efficiency_emilia# insists on a fully automated and governed drift monitoring system to protect business KPIs, while #reliability_ruth# argues that manual weekly reviews are sufficient and cheaper. #efficiency_emilia# has set a red line requiring automated governance for any future drift detection.
challenge.roundIntroduction: A recent data shift went unnoticed for three days, causing a spike in user complaints. The incident exposed that the drift monitoring workflow is currently non-functional and needs immediate repair.

on_enter_ops.reason: The drift detection script crashed due to a schema change

stalemate_ops.reason: The data feed to the drift monitor was disconnected

roster.name: Efficiency Emilia
roster.role: Uses deep domain knowledge to define business goals, objectives, and KPIs. Aligns ML features with overarching product strategy and organizational roadmaps. Evaluates system performance, operational capability, and project costs.
roster.priorities: Applying deep domain knowledge to ensure models fulfill specific business goals. Aligning ML solutions with clear objectives, KPIs, and business goals. Making organization-level decisions and enhancing overall operational capability. Defining products by defining and optimizing product features.

roster.name: Reliability Ruth
roster.role: Develops the end-user applications and services that integrate ML models. Handles model deployment, configuration, and continuous monitoring of real-world performance. Employs feedback loops to facilitate iterative improvements and system reliability.
roster.priorities: Pushes the delivery of reliable ML-powered features that directly improve the user experience. CI/CD and working feedback loops. Identifying and reporting issues to facilitate iterative improvements.

roster.name: Model Monica
roster.role: Specializes in designing, optimizing, and training machine learning models. Conducts data exploration and iterates on models to maximize predictive performance. Collaborates on model deployment, versioning, and performance monitoring.
roster.priorities: Optimizing, deploying, and monitoring high-performing ML models. Maximizing predictive performance of models. Exploring new algorithms and features.

roster.name: Requirements Reuben
roster.role: Architects secure and scalable production ML systems. Defines security requirements, ensures privacy compliance, and manages data governance. Conducts rigorous testing and validation to guarantee high product quality.
roster.priorities: Guaranteeing high product quality through rigorous testing of applications. Guaranteeing the integrity, confidentiality, and security of all ML assets. Meeting internal and external compliance and data protection standards. Keeping infrastructure stable, reproducible, and cost-controlled.

items.fact: {efficiency_emilia} proposed that any future drift detection setup requires automated governance.

readings.driver: She wants the governance layer to be as extensive as possible to cover all business KPIs.
readings.boundary: She will not approve a drift monitoring plan unless it includes automated governance controls.
readings.trade_off: She would accept manual governance if the automated version delays the launch.
readings.fact: That is simply the current policy for new monitoring features.

items.fact: {reliability_ruth} noted that manual weekly reviews are sufficient for drift monitoring.

readings.driver: She wants the weekly review process to be more detailed to catch more issues.
readings.boundary: She will not accept an automated drift monitoring system that removes the manual weekly review step.
readings.trade_off: She would give up the weekly review if the automated system is fully governed.
readings.fact: That is simply how the team currently handles drift checks.

items.fact: {efficiency_emilia} asked for a fully automated and governed drift monitoring system.

readings.driver: The more automated the drift detection, the better the protection of business KPIs.
readings.boundary: She will not present to the board without a governed drift monitoring system.
readings.trade_off: She would give up automation if the cost exceeds the budget.
readings.fact: That is simply what the current business strategy requires.

items.fact: {reliability_ruth} mentioned that manual reviews are cheaper than automated systems.

readings.driver: She wants the cost of drift monitoring to be as low as possible.
readings.boundary: She will not accept any increase in the monitoring budget.
readings.trade_off: She would accept higher costs for drift monitoring if it improves reliability.
readings.fact: That is simply the current cost structure of the monitoring setup.

items.fact: {model_monica} suggested that better drift detection would help model performance.

readings.driver: The more accurate the drift detection, the better the model retraining triggers.
readings.boundary: She will not deploy new models without drift detection.
readings.trade_off: She would give up drift detection if it slows down model iteration.
readings.fact: That is simply the current state of model monitoring.

items.fact: {requirements_reuben} proposed that drift monitoring must meet compliance standards.

readings.driver: He wants the compliance coverage of drift monitoring to be as broad as possible.
readings.boundary: He will not approve a drift monitoring setup that lacks compliance sign-off.
readings.trade_off: He would accept partial compliance if the full sign-off is delayed.
readings.fact: That is simply the current compliance requirement for monitoring systems.

items.fact: The production drift monitoring pipeline is currently non-functional.

readings.driver: Someone on the team wants the pipeline to be fully automated.
readings.boundary: The team will not accept a broken pipeline in production.
readings.trade_off: The team would accept a temporary manual workaround if the pipeline is fixed soon.
readings.fact: That is simply how the drift monitoring pipeline works today.

items.fact: The drift to alerting workflow has no trigger set.

readings.driver: Someone on the team wants the alerting to be triggered automatically.
readings.boundary: The team will not accept alerts that are not triggered by drift events.
readings.trade_off: The team would accept manual alerting if the automated trigger is complex.
readings.fact: That is simply how the drift to alerting workflow is configured today.

items.fact: The serving to observability workflow is triggered by manual request.

readings.driver: Someone on the team wants the observability to be triggered automatically.
readings.boundary: The team will not accept manual triggers for observability in production.
readings.trade_off: The team would accept manual triggers if the automated trigger is unreliable.
readings.fact: That is simply how the serving to observability workflow is configured today.

items.fact: The retraining trigger mechanism is currently absent.

readings.driver: Someone on the team wants the retraining trigger to be fully automated.
readings.boundary: The team will not accept a retraining process without a trigger.
readings.trade_off: The team would accept a manual retraining process if the trigger is not critical.
readings.fact: That is simply how the retraining trigger mechanism is set up today.
